title: Immunomodulatory Effects of Acupuncture: Changes in Cytokine Profiles in Healthy Participants
summary:
The aim of this research project is to investigate whether standardized acupuncture treatment in healthy adults induces measurable changes in the immune system. We are particularly interested in so-called cytokines. Cytokines are the body’s own signaling molecules that play an important role in regulating inflammatory responses and immune defense. Changes in these signaling molecules could provide clues as to how acupuncture affects the body.
As part of the study, participants will receive five acupuncture treatments on five consecutive days.
Blood samples will be collected to analyze the impact of acupuncture treatment on the immune system. In addition, participants will complete selected questionnaires to assess the impact of acupuncture treatment on their well-being and individual stress levels.
The findings are intended to help better understand the mechanisms of action of acupuncture and to establish a scientific foundation for future studies involving patients with inflammatory or chronic conditions.
conditions: Healthy participants / Immunomodulatory Effects of Acupuncture

interventions.name:
Standardized acupuncture treatment conducted in healthy participants.
Five sessions of 20 minutes each executed on five consecutive days.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Healthy participants without known acute or chronic conditions
- Normal complete blood count and unremarkable clinical examination
- Body Mass Index (BMI) between 18.5 and 29.9 kg/m²
- Signed informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute or chronic inflammatory, infectious, or autoimmune conditions
- Current or regular use of medications that affect the immune system, inflammatory     
   response, or endocrine system (e.g., corticosteroids, NSAIDs, antidepressants)
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Chronic pain syndromes or psychiatric disorders
- Known allergies to acupuncture needles or metals, adhesives, or disinfectants
- Acupuncture treatment within 3 months prior to inclusion in the study
- Alcohol or substance use disorder
- Participation in another clinical trial within the past 3 months
- Refusal of blood sampling or inadequate venous access
- Language barrier
